businessRequirements.title: Table 005 is present on every transaction request
businessRequirements.statement: Segment 111 shall carry exactly one Variable Information record for Table ID 005 (POS Entry Mode) on every transaction, including EMV, magnetic-stripe and key-entered transactions from all POS devices.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix I. Variable Information Data Layouts - Point-of-Service Entry Mode Information (Table ID 005)
sourceEvidence.quote: Note: The POS Entry Mode field must be populated for all transactions, which include EMV, Magstripe, and Key Entered transactions from all POS devices for any given solution.

businessRequirements.title: POS Entry Mode is selected by Table ID / Element 111 value 005
businessRequirements.statement: The POS Entry Mode record shall be identified by the three-digit Variable Information Indicator 005.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix I. Variable Information Data Layouts - Point-of-Service Entry Mode Information (Table ID 005)
sourceEvidence.quote: Table ID n Fixed value: 005

sourceEvidence.section: 13 Element No. 111 Variable Information Indicator
sourceEvidence.quote: 005 Point-of-service entry mode indicator

businessRequirements.title: Table 005 declares a fixed length of 3
businessRequirements.statement: The Table 005 record shall declare Table Length 003 for its fixed three-character data.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix I. Variable Information Data Layouts - Point-of-Service Entry Mode Information (Table ID 005)
sourceEvidence.quote: Table Length n 3 Table Data n Fixed Len.: 3

businessRequirements.title: POS Entry Mode is a 3-digit code
businessRequirements.statement: Table 005 data shall be exactly three numeric digits: PAN Entry Mode in positions 1-2 and Terminal Capability Mode in position 3.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: A valid 3-digit Point-of-Service Entry Mode code has the following components: • 2-digit PAN Entry Mode code in position nos. 1–2 • 1-digit Terminal Capability Mode code in position no. 3

businessRequirements.title: Positions 1-2 are a source-listed PAN Entry Mode code
businessRequirements.statement: Positions 1-2 shall be one of the Valid PAN Entry Mode Codes listed in Appendix J.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Valid PAN Entry Mode Codes Pos. Nos. 1–2 Description

businessRequirements.title: Position 3 is a source-listed Terminal PIN Entry Capability code
businessRequirements.statement: Position 3 shall be one of the Valid Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode Codes listed in Appendix J.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Position 3 Description

businessRequirements.title: POS Entry Mode persists through the transaction lifecycle
businessRequirements.statement: A follow-on transaction shall carry the original transaction's POS Entry Mode value, except where Appendix J defines an exception.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Note: The POS Entry Mode values listed below must persist throughout the lifecycle of the transactions, except as noted below the Valid PAN Entry Mode Codes table.

businessRequirements.title: Voids and Completions reuse the original PAN Entry Mode
businessRequirements.statement: Voids and Completions of previously authorized credit and debit transactions shall use the same PAN Entry Mode code as the original Purchase or Authorization.
businessRequirements.networkScope: Credit authorizers and debit authorizers; EBT unconfirmed

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Due to credit authorizer (American Express, Diners Club®, Discover® Network, JCB®, MasterCard®, MasterCard® Fleet, Visa®, and Visa® Fleet) and debit authorizer regulatory requirements regarding storage of full track data

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: previously authorized credit and debit transactions (Voids and Completions) can only pass the account number and expiration date to BUYPASS.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: These transactions will use the same PAN Entry Mode code as their corresponding original Purchase or Authorization transaction, with one exception:

businessRequirements.title: Voids and Completions of a 90 original use 02
businessRequirements.statement: A Void or Completion that references an original Purchase or Authorization sent with PAN Entry Mode 90 shall use PAN Entry Mode 02.
businessRequirements.networkScope: Credit authorizers and debit authorizers; EBT unconfirmed

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: previously authorized credit and debit transactions (Voids and Completions) can only pass the account number and expiration date to BUYPASS.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: They will use a PAN Entry Mode code 02 when referencing an original Purchase or Authorization transaction in which a PAN Entry Mode code 90 was used.

businessRequirements.title: Entry Mode 10 is limited to stored-credential transactions on listed brands
businessRequirements.statement: PAN Entry Mode 10 shall be used only when a transaction is initiated from credentials already stored on file, and is source-listed for Visa Credit, MasterCard Credit, Discover Credit and Amex.
businessRequirements.networkScope: VISA/MASTERCARD/DISCOVER credit and AMEX; other groups review

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Entry Mode 10 is applicable to Visa Credit, MasterCard Credit, Discover Credit, and Amex transactions where merchant or cardholder is initiating a transaction based on the credentials already stored on the file.

businessRequirements.title: The first credential-storing transaction does not use 10
businessRequirements.statement: The first transaction that verifies or stores credentials shall send the original POS Entry Mode, not PAN Entry Mode 10.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: The value is NOT applicable to the first transaction where credentials are being verified or stored.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix Z. Stored Credential
sourceEvidence.quote: The original POS Entry mode (for example: 02, 90 etc. respectively as defined in Appendix J) will be sent

businessRequirements.title: Debit Completions/Reversals after a credit COF original use 10
businessRequirements.statement: A subsequent Debit Completion or Debit Reversal whose original was initiated as a Credit COF transaction shall carry PAN Entry Mode 10.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: The value is also applicable to the subsequent Debit Completions and Debit Reversals when the original transaction was initiated as a Credit COF transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Subsequent COF transactions use 10
businessRequirements.statement: A subsequent credential-on-file transaction (COF indicator 'C') shall send PAN Entry Mode 10.
businessRequirements.networkScope: VISA/MASTERCARD/DISCOVER credit and AMEX; other groups review

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix I. Variable Information Data Layouts - Table ID 049 Sub Table ID 02
sourceEvidence.quote: POS Entry Mode 10 should be used for all subsequent COF transactions (when the COF indicator is ‘C’).

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix Z. Stored Credential
sourceEvidence.quote: For all card types, POS Entry Mode value of ‘10’ must be submitted in Data Element 111, Table ID 05 - Point-of-Service Entry Mode

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix Z. Stored Credential
sourceEvidence.quote: The use cases apply to Visa, MasterCard, Discover, and Amex.

businessRequirements.title: Discover QR/Bar/Payment Code transactions do not use 10
businessRequirements.statement: For Discover, PAN Entry Mode 10 shall not be present on QR Code, Bar Code or Payment Code transactions.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: For Discover, POS Entry Mode ‘10’ must NOT be present in the following scenarios:

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: QR Code/Bar Code/Payment Code transactions

businessRequirements.title: Discover issuer-stored or wallet-provisioned sales do not use 10
businessRequirements.statement: For Discover, PAN Entry Mode 10 shall not be present on card sales whose account information is stored by an issuer or provisioned in a digital wallet.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: For Discover, POS Entry Mode ‘10’ must NOT be present in the following scenarios:

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Card Sales with card account information stored by an Issuer or provisioned in a digital wallet

businessRequirements.title: Discover stored-credential transactions do not use 82
businessRequirements.statement: For Discover, PAN Entry Mode 82 shall not be assigned when the cardholder uses stored card account information.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: For Discover, Entry Mode 82 must NOT be assigned to card transactions for which the cardholder uses their stored card account information.

businessRequirements.title: Discover credential-on-file transactions use 10
businessRequirements.statement: Discover credential-on-file transactions shall use PAN Entry Mode 10.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: Discover Credential on File transactions must use the POS Entry Mode value of '10'.

businessRequirements.title: Contactless MSR without chip uses capability 8
businessRequirements.statement: When a contactless MSR is attached and the POS device has no chip capability, position 3 shall be 8.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: If a Contactless MSR is attached to the POS device and it has no chip capability, then all transactions will use Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode code 8

businessRequirements.title: Chip-capable (EMV) devices never use capability 8
businessRequirements.statement: An EMV contact/contactless capable device shall not send position 3 value 8; 8 is reserved for contactless MSR only.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: For EMV Contact and Contactless the valid PIN Entry Capability Mode code is 1 and not 8. The PIN Entry Capability Mode code 8 is reserved only for Contactless MSR

businessRequirements.title: PIN-debit-enabled device without contactless MSR uses capability 1
businessRequirements.statement: When no contactless MSR is attached and the PIN debit feature is enabled, position 3 shall be 1.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: If no Contactless MSR is attached, and the POS device has the PIN debit feature enabled, then all transactions will use Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode code 1

businessRequirements.title: PIN-debit-disabled device without contactless MSR uses capability 2
businessRequirements.statement: When no contactless MSR is attached and the PIN debit feature is disabled, position 3 shall be 2.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: If no Contactless MSR is attached, and the POS device has the PIN debit feature disabled, then all transactions will use Terminal PIN Entry Capability Mode code 2.

businessRequirements.title: Capability 3 is limited to MasterCard Mobile POS
businessRequirements.statement: Position 3 value 3 shall be used only on MasterCard Mobile POS transactions.
businessRequirements.networkScope: MASTERCARD; named non-MasterCard networks reject; generic groups review

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: PIN entry capability mode code 3 is applicable only to MasterCard Mobile POS transactions.

businessRequirements.title: mPOS with a PIN pad uses capability 1
businessRequirements.statement: A phone/tablet mPOS device with a dongle that has a PIN pad shall send position 3 value 1.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: mPOS Devices Phone/Tablet + Dongle with PIN Pad should have PIN Entry Capability Mode code as 1.

businessRequirements.title: mPOS without a PIN pad uses capability 3
businessRequirements.statement: A phone/tablet mPOS device with a dongle that has no PIN pad shall send position 3 value 3.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix J. Valid Point-of-Service Entry Mode Codes
sourceEvidence.quote: mPOS Devices Phone/Tablet + Dongle without PIN Pad should have PIN Entry Capability Mode code as 3.

businessRequirements.title: An attached RFID receiver requires a correct POS Entry Mode on every transaction
businessRequirements.statement: When an RFID receiver is present, every transaction request (including swiped, keyed and non-RFID card types) shall populate POS Entry Mode with the value that matches the actual entry method.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.1.5 Radio Frequency Identification Service
sourceEvidence.quote: Even if the transaction is swiped, manually keyed, or uses a card type for which RFID is not applicable, Point-of-Sale Entry Mode must be populated correctly in the transaction request from the point-of-sale when an RFID receiver is present.

businessRequirements.title: Bar-code-scanned gift cards use PAN Entry Mode 01
businessRequirements.statement: A bar-code-scanned gift card transaction shall be sent as a manual transaction with PAN Entry Mode 01.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.7.2.2 Manual Entry/Bar Code
sourceEvidence.quote: Bar Code Scanned Gift card should be treated as a manually entered transaction.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.7.2.2 Manual Entry/Bar Code
sourceEvidence.quote: The entry mode should be “01”.

businessRequirements.title: Blackhawk scanned transactions use PAN Entry Mode 90
businessRequirements.statement: A Blackhawk scanned gift card transaction shall be treated as swiped and carry PAN Entry Mode 90.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.7.2.2 Manual Entry/Bar Code
sourceEvidence.quote: The entry mode should be received as “90” for Blackhawk Scanned transactions.

businessRequirements.title: EMV fallback swipe uses PAN Entry Mode 80
businessRequirements.statement: When the device is EMV enabled, the card is a chip card and the card is swiped, the original request shall carry PAN Entry Mode 80.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.14.4 EMV Fallback Transaction Processing
sourceEvidence.quote: Regardless, a Fallback will occur whenever an EMV Certified solution cannot read or obtain a viable matching AID.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.14.4 EMV Fallback Transaction Processing
sourceEvidence.quote: Always send the Fallback Entry Mode of ‘80’or spec equivalent

businessRequirements.title: Non-chip or non-chip-capable swipe uses PAN Entry Mode 90
businessRequirements.statement: When the card is not a chip card or the device is not chip capable and the card is swiped, the original request shall carry PAN Entry Mode 90.

sourceEvidence.section: 10.14.4 EMV Fallback Transaction Processing
sourceEvidence.quote: Send as a MSR Entry Mode of ‘90’or spec equivalent

businessRequirements.title: Tokenized transactions carry a POS Entry Mode for token presentment
businessRequirements.statement: A tokenized transaction shall carry a valid Appendix J POS Entry Mode indicating the token presentment mode; which codes represent token presentment is not source-defined.

sourceEvidence.section: Appendix O. Payment Token Terminologies
sourceEvidence.quote: A value that is used to indicate the token presentment mode through which the token is presented for payment.

clarificationQuestions.question: Should PAN Entry Mode 10 assertions be considered applicable to STAR Signature Debit and generic Debit beyond the explicit Appendix J footnote wording?
Do you want lifecycle persistence (BR-POSEM-010) to include Reversal with the same 90->02 exception, or keep exception scope strictly to Voids/Completions?
When lifecycle follows an original with missing/invalid capability digit, should capability persistence remain review-only or be an explicit failure?
Appendix J footnote 1 lists credit/debit authorizers but not EBT. Should EBT inherit the same lifecycle persistence and 90->02 exception?
Capability code 3 is MasterCard mPOS-specific. For other networks/generic groups, should this be FAIL or REVIEW_REQUIRED until network supplements are approved?
For MasterCard non-mPOS traffic, should capability code 3 be treated as hard fail or conditional review?
Appendix O defines token presentment mode conceptually but does not map concrete Table 005 values. Which code(s) are approved for each token presentment channel?
Appendix J code 04 row combines barcode scan and OCR-for-EMV wording. Should these be split into separate operational constraints?
When fallback-to-swipe conditions are met but EMV payload still appears, should this be modeled as a separate BR failure or a lifecycle-level conflict?
Table 005 is required for all transactions. Please confirm if any host/program exceptions exist that intentionally omit Segment 111.
Appendix J footnote 2 references subsequent Debit Completions/Reversals after Credit COF. Confirm this applies to STAR Signature Debit in your implementation.
For Discover exclusions under code 10, do your QR/bar/payment-code and wallet flows include additional sub-conditions not captured in ATL105 text?
